No easy way to cook using indirect heat with design but knew that before buying. Uses disposable propane bottles but I bought adapter to use my full size propane tank with 5 ft hose and save bottles. Highly recommend if you need smaller and/or portable grill that looks good and cooks great.

Results.ReviewText:
I bought this Weber Q1200 grill for use with my RV camping. There are so many grills to choose from this was the one with the most positive reviews and my brother has had his Q for 15 years. So, I thought I would give it a try. 
I love this grill. It cooks evenly once it heats up and it is easy to clean. It’s worth taking the time to clean it when done. I highly recommend the Q if you need a small portable grill.
Results.Title: Great portable grill for the RV

Results.ReviewText: The Q 1200 ultimately is portable and capable.  The issue I have is with the propane bottle attachment.  The instructions recommend the use of 14 or 16 oz propane bottles for this grill.  I can find 100 16 oz bottles to every 14 oz bottle on store shelves.  My preference would be to use the more available and less costly, per unit, 16 oz bottles.  The 16 oz bottle however requires you to bend the regulator top accommodate the diameter of the bottle.  This appears to me to be a bad idea and probable contribute to a long term failure of the fuel delivery system.  I was told by Weber that it was okay and if I had a problem, use a 20 lb bottle.  That makes the unit no longer portable.  How sad that Weber would develop a product with such an inappropriate configuration.
Results.Title: Propane bottles

Results.ReviewText: Worked great first time as it is new.  Cooked steaks just like. directions said.
Results.Title: Worked great first time

As with all grills you need to learn the hot spots but it has been working excellent.  I did however purchase a 5’ propane hose with a gauge for 15$ on Amazon so i could use my three 20lb takes that a had from my late grill.  Well worth it!

A couple of our camping friends had one, and we watched how well it worked, and decided to try one, so now we have two.  The feature on the new one with the split grate is a excellent feature, as we bought the optional flat plate for breaded fish, and things like that.

The girls at Weber that I talked to we’re so helpful in determining as to what model I had, they sent the right one the first time. Thank you girls for spending so much time on this.
The only question I have is how hot is this grill capable of ? Mine gets to 425 degrees, but takes awhile to get there according to the gauge on the cover.

Results.ReviewText: Purchased based on 2 friends being very happy with theirs.  Converted to low pressure gas and it works very well.  Wish Weber would consider offering this option since new RV's come with low pressure connections and there are not many choices.  I use it for home and camping!

Results.ReviewText: A few years ago, I spent a summer working at Lowes assembling outdoor grills.  By the end of that summer it became clear to me....there where Weber grills, and then there where all the rest.  The Weber grills are far better quality and very well engineered.  A buddy of mine bought the Q2200 and I got to use it and I loved it.  So when I saw a great deal on the Q1200, I jumped on it.  I love it and I've increased my grilling time largely because of it.  Probably the last grill I'll ever need.  I Highly, Highly recommend trying out the Q series.
